title: React and React Hooks (useState & useEffect)
summary: Moves from changing the DOM by hand to React's state-driven model. useState stores data that triggers a re-render when it changes (updated immutably with spread and filter); useEffect runs side effects like API requests, and its dependency array controls when it runs, with cleanup on unmount. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Manage component data with useState and run side effects with useEffect, choosing the right dependency array.

steps.title: Read both hook lessons
steps.detail: Read 'The useState Hook' and 'The useEffect Hook', especially 'Why the Dependency Array Matters' and the mounting / re-rendering / unmounting section.
steps.doneWhen: You can say what [], [someState] and no array each mean for an effect.

steps.title: Read your own hooks in Myflix
steps.detail: You already use both hooks. Open assignments/week-02/netflix/src/hooks/useMyList.js: it uses useState for syncStatus and has three useEffect calls. For each effect, write down its dependencies and whether it returns a cleanup function.
steps.doneWhen: You have a short note explaining when each of the three effects runs.

steps.title: Watch an effect run
steps.detail: Drop the lesson's first effect into any component in a scratch Vite app, then try it with [] and with no array. In development, React's StrictMode runs effects twice on mount on purpose, so you may see two logs.
steps.doneWhen: With [] it logs on load only; with no array it logs after every render.

steps.title: Spot immutable updates
steps.detail: The lesson adds to state with spread ([...old, item]) and removes with filter. Search assignments/week-02/netflix/src for '...' and '.filter(' and find one place Myflix updates state this way.
steps.doneWhen: You found one spread or filter state update in Myflix.

concepts.meaning: Data a component remembers between renders; changing it re-renders the component.
React running your component again to update the screen.
A hook for side effects like fetching data, timers or subscriptions.
The list after an effect that decides when it re-runs.
Making a new array or object instead of changing the old one, so React notices.
